statement: Network baseline learning runs in a learning mode that completes automatically when the rate of newly learned behaviour falls below a threshold, or after a fixed window, and can be completed or reset manually.
An anomaly can be acknowledged as learned, which adds the observed behaviour to the device baseline so the same behaviour no longer alerts.
Devices designated as scanners (authorised scanning tools) do not raise scan anomalies; the designation is an explicit, audited asset attribute.

Device records discovered through several identifiers (MAC, hostname, serial, client id, TLS fingerprint) are consolidated into one asset; consolidation and splitting are explicit operations with evidence.
Classification confidence is expressed as tiers (high, medium, low) with documented thresholds, and the tier gates automatic policy assignment.
Segmentation policy recommendations are generated per device group from the learned behaviour of high-confidence member devices only, and are reviewed before activation.
Each safe active query is enabled per tenant and query type, and honours blackout windows during which no query runs.

Active queries exclude restricted address ranges, categories and device types, are limited per target per day, require approval above safe risk or for safety-sensitive devices, and are rate limited on the edge.
module: iot-core activeq.rs (plan); edge/activeq.rs (rate limit, intrusive refusal)

statement: Network learning and process-variable learning run independently, so process learning can be restarted without discarding the network baseline.
Written process values are learned as per-variable ranges and values outside the learned range raise anomalies.
Administrators define assertions over the inventory in a bounded expression language; assertions are evaluated continuously and violations are listed and alertable.
Zones with security levels and the conduits between them (observed zone-to-zone communication with protocols and highest operation class) are first-class objects of segmentation.
Baselines are snapshotted before every change and a snapshot can be compared with the current baseline (edges added/removed, operation classes raised, value ranges changed).
Administrators save inventory views (filters, expression, columns) and share them.
Vulnerability findings can be acknowledged with a mandatory reason (risk acceptance), resolved and reopened; acknowledgement is audited.
Use of cleartext credentials (Telnet, FTP, HTTP Basic, SNMP communities, MQTT/AMQP passwords) is reported as a finding without retaining the credential.
module: iot-core vuln.rs (cleartext credentials); collect.rs; protocols/snmp.rs (community redaction)

statement: Risk factor weights and thresholds are tunable per tenant within validated bounds; every score lists the contributing factors.
An operational impact score (device criticality, safety sensitivity, site criticality) is computed separately from likelihood and combined into a remediation priority.
module: iot-core risk.rs (impact, priority); api/assets.rs (sort by priority)

statement: Device identity is multi-dimensional: category, type, vendor, model, operating system and firmware are classified with separate confidences.
Assets follow an explicit lifecycle (discovered, active, inactive, merged, decommissioned); inactivity is detected automatically and decommissioning removes the device from policy.
Remote access to OT assets is granted only for just-in-time windows with a maximum length and advance limit; sessions cannot start outside the window and are ended at its end.
Vendor principals (external maintainers) request access themselves or through automation; the asset owner approves in the approval inbox and the requester can never approve their own request.
Credentials of target devices are held by the access broker (privileged consoles); vendors never receive them.
Administrators see live sessions and can terminate any session immediately; revocation of a request ends its sessions and the broker grant.
Session recordings are referenced by metadata with a SHA-256 integrity digest, size and duration; recording content stays with the broker.
The inventory exports to CSV and JSON with the same filters as the list, with formula-injection neutralisation.
Data-quality diagnostics show classification conflicts, ambiguous identities and stale assets so administrators can resolve them.
Alerts are de-duplicated per device and kind, counted, and can be acknowledged or resolved; tuning (learned behaviour, scanner designation) suppresses known-good activity.
Temporary, specific segmentation exceptions (devices or groups, protocol, port, highest operation class) need approval by someone other than the requester and expire automatically within 30 days.
Engineering operations (program download/upload, firmware update, configuration changes) are detected per protocol and attributed to the initiating station.
Controller mode changes (stop, run, restart, cold/warm start) raise high-severity anomalies.
Quarantine is enforced through the enforcement points (edge decisions and nftables drops, firewall identity bindings) and is reversible and audited.
Programming or write operations from stations not learned as engineering stations for the controller are flagged as unauthorised engineering activity.
A topology and dependency map shows devices, their peers, protocols and Purdue levels, and answers which devices depend on a given device.
Tenant threat indicators (IP addresses, domains) with expiry are matched against device communication and raise threat-intelligence anomalies that raise risk.
The edge appliance keeps enforcing its last verified configuration when the cloud is unreachable, buffers observations in a bounded queue, and refuses tampered configuration.
